summary.title: Awk in 20 Minutes
summary.one_liner: Awk is a small pattern-action language for processing line-based text such as server logs, and this guide walks through its execution model, data types, patterns, fields, actions, functions and special variables.
keywords: awk special variables fs rs ofs ors
analyze text files with command line
takeaways: Awk runs a sequence of pattern { action } pairs against every input line, one line at a time.
Awk has two basic data types (strings and numbers), global variables, and associative arrays declared on the fly.
Patterns can be regular expressions, Boolean expressions, or the special BEGIN and END blocks; fields $0, $1, $2 etc. split each line by whitespace by default.
Awk is useful for log parsing and transforming text on servers, going beyond what grep does by also processing data.
The author shows a real example parsing Erlang crash dumps to list processes with large message queues.
summary.summary: The article is a quick introduction to Awk, aimed at using it for log parsing on servers. It explains the pattern-action execution model, the two data types, regex and Boolean patterns, the BEGIN and END special patterns, and how fields ($0, $1, ...) work. It then covers common actions, global variables, user-defined functions and special variables such as FS, RS, OFS and ORS. The author closes with a real script that parses Erlang crash dumps to list functions with oversized process mailboxes.
